scope: Real community MCP runtime installation and integration, not ChatGPT UI hookup or discovery product
execution_environment: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04; real non-root Docker runtime; integration containers have network none

checks.count_note: Counts belong to different checks, not a single benchmark. Repeated HTTP tests are not unique tests.

verified: Read current project files and write actual files through the real SpaceDock MCP server
Run both existing project test and demo tasks through MCP, not a fake responder
Observe one long command session until exit without launching a duplicate command
Root-scoped recall does not mix the two separately configured project roots
Explicit shared recall root denies its structured command tool
File traversal through the structured file tool is denied
Worktree changes do not change the source checkout
Recall and files persist after actual MCP server restart
User-facing Compose installation profile passes HTTP OAuth and command checks
Named-volume data survives container removal and recreation
Actual workbench doctor succeeds under the selected Python
MCP file change is committed to Git in a disposable fixture and recovered in a fresh local clone

earlier_runs.result: Original container build and upstream HTTP checks passed; own project exercise absent then
Workflow definition failed before any jobs; runner-scoped path initialization moved to a step
23 real MCP project checks and installation profile passed; later audit found Python 3.11 versus workbench 3.12 contract gap

not_done: ChatGPT custom MCP authorization and tool call
Goal/Loop execution against a real model
Remote Git push from the runtime
security_boundary: Per-root memory separation is logical. Trusted shell commands share the container OS user and can reach other paths in that container. This is not hostile-tenant isolation or a complete security audit.
build_reproducibility: Upstream source commits pinned. Base image tags and apt repositories are not fully digest-locked.
record_note: This result is recorded after the tested commit. A subsequent metadata change does not retroactively become part of that test.
